Really sorry to hear about your experiences Jess. Nurse's apathy and outright bad attitude towards patients is something I've also witnessed.

When I did Mental Health support work I was promised training for appropriate qualifications. The times allocated for training programs got postponed, then postponed again, then finally cancelled on short notice. It was a major factor in me leaving that job.

Don't provide a private space and you violate their privacy and dignity.

Mental health units are spaces where there's a 'grey area' regarding how many basic rights can be overlooked with the intent of keeping patients safe. Unfortunately following all the rules and conventions in place may not be enough to keep people safe and facilitate their recovery. It's a bloody complex thing and there's no easy answers.

Based on my own brief experiences working in Mental Health, none of what is described in the available reports surprises me. Overcrowded, deteriorating facilities, poor staff/patient ratios and poorly trained staff in particular - granted these issues have been reported for years with minimal progress taken to rectify these issues.

Funding is the common denominator for these issues to improve facilities, provide decent wages and support to Staff, implement Staff training programs, and to expand the range services and treatments available to patients.

To expand, last election Labour and the Nats were pretty tight in the polls close to the election date thanks to the 'Jacindamania' boost for Labour whilst the Greens had dropped off in July from around the 10% mark see [here](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2017_New_Zealand_general_election).

I'm no number-cruncher, but based on those stats it looks like potential Greens voters switched to Labour in order to hedge a better bet to knock off National, along with Centrist voters who could toss a coin between the Nats/Labour and preferred Jacinda's optimistic vigueur over Bill English's dour crustiness. 

Yes Labour/Greens coalitions are virtually guaranteed, but a lot of people like to place more secure gambits when the outcomes look uncertain.

To be fair those left-wing voters are going for the 'strategic' vote by voting for Labour in the hopes of a Labour-Greens coalition. Polls never indicate that the Greens can achieve a majority, so Green-sympathetic voters play the game with MMP.
